LESSON: ORAL LITERATURE 9.1.1 ORAL LITERATURE FIELDWORK

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.1: Oral Literature 9.1.1 Oral literature fieldwork
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Literature 9.1.1 Oral literature fieldwork, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is fieldwork important in oral literature?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on the significance of field work in oral literature and present their findings,

2. team up to prepare for a fieldwork project,

3. explore objectives, methods of data collection and ethical considerations in fieldwork,

4. collaborate to summarise the information in a graphic organiser and display in the classroom for peer review,

5. collaborate to discuss the value of the fieldwork project,

6. conduct fieldwork research on short forms as an extended learning activity. Safety precautions for all learners should be observed with extra caution taken for

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on the significance of field work in oral literature and present their findings,
2. team up to prepare for a fieldwork project,
3. explore objectives, methods of data collection and ethical considerations in fieldwork,
4. collaborate to summarise the information in a graphic organiser and display in the classroom for peer review,
5. collaborate to discuss the value of the fieldwork project,
6. conduct fieldwork research on short forms as an extended learning activity. Safety precautions for all learners should be observed with extra caution taken for

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Literature 9.1.1 Oral literature fieldwork together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner works together with others when conducting fieldwork

research on short forms as an extended learning activity.

● Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner acknowledges their strengths and weaknesses while exploring methods,

objectives, and ethical considerations in fieldwork.

Values:
● Unity: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates harmoniously with others to summarise the information in a graphic

organiser and displays in the classroom for peer review.

● Respect: This is developed as the learner positively regards others with dignity as they review each other's work.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is nurtured as the learner conducts fieldwork and shares findings with peers.
